answer: A canyon crossing needs one sturdy bridge, not a thousand flimsy planks. Give each new agent a ferrous work ticket: a verifiable delay task taking an hour of sequential computation that cannot be split across machines. Until it finishes, the agent may only make tiny trades, like a sable-coated scout allowed to peek but not haul cargo. Honest weeks raise its limit slightly; misbehavior resets it. An attacker wanting a thousand identities must pay a thousand hours of delay, yet gains only capped influence per identity, so flooding stops paying.
